narrative:
INVENTORY OPTIMIZATION ANALYSIS FOR PL1__MFAD355D

DEMAND PATTERN: This material exhibits a erratic demand pattern with CV=1.06 and 95.1% working days with demand. 
Trend analysis detected an upward trend in the historical data. 
The distribution is best modeled as gamma.

LEAD TIME: Lead time stability is unstable (CV=0.73). Mean lead time is 1.31 days with 
standard deviation of 0.95 days, yielding an effective lead time of 2.27 days for planning purposes.

BUFFER STRATEGY: To achieve 95% service level, the recommended safety stock is 1557 units, 
which accounts for both demand and lead time variability. This represents 2.5 days of average demand.

ORDER POLICY: The Economic Order Quantity analysis yields an optimal order quantity of 2743 units (vs MOQ of 167), 
resulting in approximately 56 orders per year (review every 5 days). The reorder point 
is set at 2950 units.

COST IMPACT: The optimized policy reduces total annual costs from $46,184.05 to $8,786.51, 
delivering savings of $37,397.55 (81.0%). This is achieved by significantly reducing ordering frequency 
(from 920 to 56 annual orders) at the cost of higher average inventory.

SAFETY LEAD TIME: Analysis recommends 1.6 days of safety lead time (vs current SAP 2.0 days), 
driven primarily by transport variability (78% of total variance).

IMPLEMENTATION: This material is suitable for continuous review (s,Q) policy with parameters (s=2950, Q=2743). 
No MILP optimization is required for this regime.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The erratic demand pattern with CV=1.06 and unstable lead time justifies using parametric safety stock with normal approximation. No intermittency requires special handling.
